member.name: T:ProtoDesigner.CodeGen.Cpp.CppGenerator
member.summary: Emits C++14 conversion code for a protocol. Output is a fixed runtime header plus one header per bus holding an enum per IR enum, a struct per message in its host representation, and the two conversions between that struct and the wire: ConvertToWire(host, wire, cap) and ConvertToHost(wire, len, host).
member.remarks: Offsets inside a region are emitted as compile-time constants. A region runs a cursor for its elements only; the fixed region that follows it goes back to constant offsets relative to where the variable part ended. That is the whole point of the region model.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.CodeGen.Cpp.CppGenerator.ToWireCode(System.String,ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.ScalarTransform,ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.PrimitiveKind)
member.summary: wire = (value - offset) / scale, wrapped in a round-to-nearest when the maths is floating-point.
member.remarks: The rounding is not cosmetic. Assigning a double to an integer truncates toward zero, so a -40..70 field scaled by 110/255 turns 70.0 into 254.99999999999997 and stores 254 — the top code the width was chosen for is never reached, and every other reading is biased low by up to a full code. Integer pipelines are left alone: forcing them through a double would lose precision above 2^53 for no gain.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.CodeGen.Cpp.CppGenerator.FromWireCode(System.String,ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.ScalarTransform,ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.PrimitiveKind)
member.summary: value = (wire * scale) + offset.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.CodeGen.Cpp.CppGenerator.IsFloatingMath(ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.ScalarTransform,ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.PrimitiveKind)
member.summary: Whether the emitted expression is evaluated in floating point: either the host is a float, or the scale is fractional and drags the whole expression into double.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.CodeGen.Cpp.CppGenerator.IsRawFloat(ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.PrimitiveKind,ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.ScalarTransform)
member.summary: A float host with no transform: the IEEE bit pattern goes on the wire untouched. The propagator guarantees the pairing — a float wire form produces no transform, and any integer wire form on a float host always produces one.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.CodeGen.Cpp.CppGenerator.Signed(System.Decimal)
member.summary: Renders a term as + n or - n, so an offset of -40 reads `+ 40`, not `- -40`.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.CodeGen.Cpp.CppGenerator.Dec(System.Decimal)
member.summary: Emits a transform constant as a C++ literal.
member.remarks: Integral values stay integral so an otherwise-integer pipeline is not forced into floating-point maths. Everything else becomes a double literal — never a float one. A derived scale is (max - min) / (2^bits - 1), which carries far more significant digits than float's ~7: rounding 110/255 down to float puts the top of a -40..70 range at 254.99999 of 255 codes, and the cast to an integer then truncates it to 254. The whole top of the range would be off by one.

member.summary: Strips characters that are illegal in a C++ identifier. Any run of illegal characters acts as a word separator and capitalises the next letter, so "sensor-array 2" becomes "sensorArray2" (or "SensorArray2" when is set). Underscores are legal and pass through, which is what keeps dotted IR paths readable after the caller rewrites '.' to '_'.

member.name: T:ProtoDesigner.CodeGen.Runtime.BitBuffer
member.summary: A bit-level buffer. Writes and reads happen at bit granularity; the buffer grows a byte at a time. This is the canonical reference implementation of the wire semantics — every generator must produce code that matches it byte for byte on any well-formed message.
member.remarks:
Encoding model:
Whole-byte scalars honour . Sub-byte scalars are always packed MSB-first in the storage byte, matching what most protocol specs describe ().
Bit-packed fields may straddle byte boundaries in Contiguous mode; the caller (validator) guarantees that the layout is legal before we get here.
This is deliberately small; generated code eventually inlines this logic.

member.name: T:ProtoDesigner.CodeGen.Runtime.ReferenceCodec
member.summary: The canonical encode/decode implementation, driven entirely by . This is what test suites use to prove the semantics — and what the WPF live preview calls to show what a sample instance would look like on the wire.
member.remarks: Values are addressed by their field . A field of scalar / enum kind holds an IConvertible number (or a ). An array field holds an of element values. That keeps this reference completely generic; a real C++/C# generator emits strongly typed structs and calls into equivalent bit operations directly.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.CodeGen.Runtime.ReferenceCodec.Quantize(System.Decimal)
member.summary: Rounds a scaled value to the nearest wire code, half away from zero — the exact rule the generated C++ applies via protodesigner::quantize. Truncating instead (which is what a plain cast to an integer does) would bias every reading down by up to a full code and put the top of a range out of reach: 70.0 on a -40..70 field scaled by 110/255 lands a hair under 255 and would store 254.
